claim_verdicts.evidence: OrdersController.cs @stage-1 (full file, read fresh this session): `Create`'s body contains no `if`/`switch`/`??`; its single `return` is `return CreatedAtAction(nameof(Get), new { id = order.Id }, ToDto(order));`. The preceding statements only read `customerId`, build `items`, and await `PlaceOrderAsync`. Mechanical diff of `git show stage-1:...OrdersController.cs | sed -n '9,28p'` against the lesson's fenced block (en.md lines 58-77) returned no differences.

RFC 9110 §9.3.3, verbatim in the local mirror: "If one or more resources has been created on the origin server as a result of successfully processing a POST request, the origin server SHOULD send a 201 (Created) response containing a Location header field that provides an identifier for the primary resource created (Section 10.2.2) and a representation that describes the status of the request while referring to the new resource(s)."

RFC 9110 §9.2.2, verbatim: "A request method is considered 'idempotent' if the intended effect on the server of multiple identical requests with that method is the same as the effect for a single such request. Of the request methods defined by this specification, PUT, DELETE, and safe request methods are idempotent." POST is absent from that list; §9.2.1 lists the safe methods as GET, HEAD, OPTIONS, TRACE, so POST is neither safe nor idempotent.

Dtos.cs @stage-1, line 13: `public sealed record CreateOrderRequest(List<CreateOrderItemRequest> Items);` — one positional parameter, no id. Line 11: `CreateOrderItemRequest(int ProductId, int Quantity, int UnitPriceVnd)` has no id either, so no id can be sent at any level of the request body.

ASP.NET Core docs: "A 201 status code is generated by the CreatedAtAction method when a product is created. In this code path, the Product object is provided in the response body. A `Location` response header containing the newly created product's URL is provided." Route source confirmed by source + execution: `OrdersController.Get` is `[HttpGet("{id:int}")]` under class-level `[Route("api/v1/orders")]`, and a live POST this session answered `Location: http://localhost:8080/api/v1/orders/19`.

claim_verdicts.evidence: OrdersController.cs @stage-1, full file: the identifier `repository` appears exactly twice — the primary constructor parameter (line 12) and `await repository.FindAsync(id)` inside `Get(int id)` (line 33). `Create` (lines 19-28) references only `orderService`; `Cancel` uses `orderService.CancelOrderAsync`. No other member touches `repository`.

db/schema.sql @stage-1, line 19: `id integer GENERATED BY DEFAULT AS IDENTITY PRIMARY KEY` in `CREATE TABLE orders`. OrderService.PlaceOrderAsync builds `new Order { ... }` with no Id, then `await repository.AddAsync(order); await repository.SaveChangesAsync();` before returning it — so the id exists only after the save, confirmed by the live runs returning ids 19 and 20.

issues.text: An absolute the pinned standard does not support. RFC 9110 §9.2.1 defines safe as intent, not guarantee: "the client does not request, and does not expect, any state change", and adds "This definition of safe methods does not prevent an implementation from including behavior that is potentially harmful, that is not entirely read-only, or that causes side effects while invoking a safe method." Section 4 repeats the absolute: "repeating a `GET` never does." True of this API's two GET methods (verified last lesson), not true of GET as such.
issues.quote: unlike a `GET`, which leaves the server exactly as it was however many times it is sent
issues.fix: Core concepts bullet 4: "— unlike a `GET`, which is not supposed to change the server at all, however many times it is sent." How it works, third paragraph: "Repeating the exact same `POST` changes the server again each time; repeating a `GET` is not supposed to change it at all." Keep the rest of both passages as they are — the effect-on-the-server framing is correct.
